transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?
Mostly, I’m here because I’m tired in a way that doesn’t really make sense. I can sleep and keep up at work, but I still feel like I’m running on a low battery before the day even gets going.
Over the past few weeks, have you noticed a persistent low or sad mood, or a loss of interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah. It’s been a long time, really—this gray, flat feeling most days. Things I used to look forward to, like fishing, working on my tomatoes, or going to a church concert, feel more like things I ought to check off than things I actually enjoy.
How long have you been feeling this way—has it been going on for two years or more, or is it more recent than that?
It’s been about two years and four months—since I got pulled back into full operational leadership.
Has anyone told you that you snore loudly, gasp, or seem to stop breathing for moments while you're asleep?
I’m not really sure. No one’s mentioned that to me.
Have you noticed any recent weight gain, feeling unusually cold, dry skin, or hair thinning?
No, I haven’t really noticed any of those things.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a variety of things—like work, health, or family—more days than not, and having trouble controlling that worry?
I’m not sure I’d say I worry excessively. I do think about work and things, but I can’t really tell if it’s more than normal.
Have you noticed feeling unusually short of breath or your heart racing when you climb stairs or do other everyday physical activity?
I haven’t really noticed that. Climbing stairs feels about the same as usual.
Over these past two years, have there been any periods where your mood or energy got noticeably worse for two weeks or more, compared to how you've been feeling generally?

I wouldn’t say there’s been a distinct stretch where it got a lot worse. It’s more this gray, flat feeling most days for a long time. Things like fishing, working on my tomatoes, or going to a church concert—they feel more like things to check off than things I actually enjoy.
Have you noticed feeling lightheaded or dizzy, or has anyone commented that you look unusually pale?
No, I haven’t noticed feeling lightheaded or dizzy. Nobody’s mentioned that I look pale, either.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports a persistent, chronic low/flat mood and anhedonia lasting over 2 years (2 years, 4 months), without a distinct 2-week period of significant worsening consistent with a major depressive episode. Screening ruled out sleep apnea, hypothyroidism, anemia, and generalized anxiety disorder as contributing medical/psychiatric explanations. The chronic, low-grade, non-episodic nature of the mood disturbance with functional impact on previously enjoyed activities (fishing, gardening, social/religious activities) is most consistent with Persistent Depressive Disorder (Dysthymia).
